On Windows, MaiCord 0.5.x through 0.8.0 install this update from Settings > Updates. If you're still on 0.4.0, follow the one-time manual steps in the [0.5.0 release notes](https://github.com/maj113/MaiCord/releases/tag/v0.5.0). On Linux, the installer and tarball installs and the AppImage update from Settings > Updates, packages through your package manager, and the musl AppImage through AppImageUpdate. MaiCord now needs an Intel Haswell (2013) or AMD Excavator (2015) or Zen (2017) processor, or newer: on Intel, a 4th generation Core i3, i5 or i7 (i3/i5/i7-4xxx) or newer.

Please update soon: a message that any Discord user can send froze MaiCord 0.8.0 and earlier (the first fix below).

### What's new

- **YouTube sounds better.** MaiCord plays YouTube's Opus audio, which goes up to 20 kHz, as the YouTube Music web player does. Before, it played the AAC format, which stops at about 16 kHz. A video with no Opus format plays AAC as before.
- **YouTube loudness.** Loud videos and tracks play at the loudness of YouTube's and YouTube Music's web players. Peaks are no longer cut off before your system volume.
- **YouTube Music art tracks play as audio.** A track with one still picture no longer downloads and decodes its video: the example track took 2.0 MB, not 5.6 MB. Audio-only tracks show a sharp 1280x720 picture instead of a stretched small one.
- **YouTube format picks.** The media page header shows the format MaiCord picked. Portrait videos no longer play at 480p. Of two formats of one size, the higher frame rate wins. A format of 4 GiB or more no longer makes the video fail.
- **Videos without a decoder say so.** A video that your computer has no decoder for showed an empty grey box. It now says why, and MaiCord stops downloading it again every minute. On Linux, H.264 video without a GPU decoder needs OpenH264: the box says "Install OpenH264 to play this video".

### Fixed in this release

- **A Thai message froze MaiCord.** A Thai letter with 255 or more marks made text layout never finish, so the window stopped responding. Any Discord user could send such a message. It lays out now.
- **Linux on Wayland, KDE Plasma and NixOS.**
  - Paste, copy, drag and drop, and input methods did not work on any Wayland desktop. The window icon and the window's handle for the desktop's dialogs failed too. All of them work now.
  - MaiCord did not start when the desktop had only some variable fonts, such as Noto Sans on NixOS or Ubuntu Sans. A broken font file could stop all text too. MaiCord now skips such a file.
  - Chinese, Japanese and Korean text showed as boxes on NixOS and Fedora, whose Noto Sans CJK is a CFF2 font. MaiCord reads it now. While the boxes showed, each look-up of the missing font took 4 to 6 ms. So the client got very slow. MaiCord now remembers a font it can't use.
  - On GNOME 48 and later, the interface used a fallback font instead of Adwaita Sans. It uses the desktop's font now.
  - Close to the tray left the window on screen, where it looked frozen. It hides now, and on KDE the taskbar shows MaiCord's icon again when the window comes back.
  - When the GPU could not start, Linux asked for Direct3D 11. It now names what it needs: OpenGL ES 3.1.
- **YouTube and other media audio on Linux.**
  - Audio skipped after the stream ran dry, for example while a download waited for the network. It now pauses and plays all of the audio.
  - With a sound server of long latency, the audio could go silent after about 2 seconds. MaiCord now queues enough audio for such a server.
  - A sound server that doesn't answer gets two more tries, 1 and 2 seconds later, while the player shows buffering. After that the player says "Sound server not answering".
  - Some AAC audio decoded with small errors.
- **YouTube Music links.** A music.youtube.com link to one track played as a YouTube video, at YouTube's lower loudness. It plays as YouTube Music now: a song with one picture plays as audio only, at the loudness of the web player.
- **Devanagari and Bengali digits.** On Windows, a message with Devanagari or Bengali digits, such as "४६", failed to lay out. Segoe UI has the digits but not the script. The chat's text could fail to draw with it. Both work now.
- **Copy and cut on the sign-in screen.** Ctrl+C and Ctrl+X now work in the login field. A password, and a sign-in link the field hides, are never copied.
- **Long runs of joiners.** A letter followed by thousands of zero-width joiners stalled the window. One Bengali line took 579 ms for each layout, and Khmer, Myanmar, Sinhala and Tibetan were slow too. Such a line now takes one pass.
- **Heavy animated stickers.** A small crafted Lottie sticker could keep the sticker decoder busy for seconds on each frame. A frame now stops at a work limit that is more than 9 times the largest frame of Discord's own sticker packs.
- **Keybinds in a call.** With the window in the background, a short press of a custom keybind, such as toggle mute, often did nothing. MaiCord now reads the keys every 20 ms.
- Streams and cameras in a call kept decoding while the window was hidden in the tray. They stop now, as they do when the window is minimized. Call audio doesn't change.
- With the Prism name effect (five colours), the profile editor failed to draw and the client kept one processor core busy. The row takes five colours now, and a frame that fails is retried at most four times a second.
- A theme that MaiCord saved could fail to load again when an effect setting's name had a control character in it.
- The chat no longer fades out above the message box while it is scrolled up. Discord's client has no such fade. With a flat theme and a background effect or Stars, the fade showed as a dark band.

### Faster and smaller

- The Windows MaiCord.exe is 6.48 MB and the Linux program 6.49 MB, both under 6.5 MB.
- No change in this release made a measured path more than 2% slower, and most measured paths are 5 to 90% faster.
- **Signing in.** The first data Discord sends after sign-in (READY) decodes in 37% less time. MaiCord also stores it in 37% less time (60 servers in our test). The updater now starts after the first frame.
- **Channel list.** Its rebuild, which runs on each unread or mention change, takes 51 to 58% less time. For a server of 26 channels among 7,700, a channel list for each server takes another 82% off.
- **Text.** Lines with capital letters lay out in 72% less time, and bold and italic lines in 45 to 62% less. Plain lower-case lines take about half the time.
- **Chat.** A scroll step of the message list takes 42% less time, and painting the visible messages 19 to 25% less. Each new message and member list update from Discord takes 10 to 30% less time to process.
- **Pictures.** JPEGs decode on the CPU in about half the time, and a new integer transform takes off another 7 to 19%. PNG photos without transparency take half the time, and lossy WebP images 30 to 35% less. A pasted 1920x1080 screenshot converts to PNG in 17 ms, not 171 ms.
- **Voice.** Mixing voices takes 71 to 87% less time, and the whole 20 ms playback step 4 to 9% less. A silent call no longer wakes the window each second.
- **Animated stickers.** A Lottie frame compiles in 38% less time.
